references.text: Jesus uses similar harvest imagery when he says the harvest is plentiful but the workers are few, and he urges his disciples to pray to the Lord of the harvest to send out workers – the same image of a spiritual harvest as in [ref:Matt 9:37-38|Matthew 9:37-38].
Also in [ref:Luk 10:2|Luke 10:2] Jesus speaks of the great harvest and the need for workers, paralleling the call to lift one's eyes and see that the fields are white for harvest.

In [ref:Ordsp 10:5|Proverbs 10:5] it is said that he who gathers in summer is a wise son, while he who sleeps during harvest brings shame – an image of seizing the opportunity, just as Jesus urges his disciples to see that the harvest is ripe now.

In [ref:Joel 3:13|Joel 3:13] the harvest image is used eschatologically: 'Swing the sickle, for the harvest is ripe!' – the same kind of harvesting metaphor Jesus uses regarding the spiritual harvest.

In [ref:Åp 14:15|Revelation 14:15] an angel cries out that the time to reap has come, for the earth's crop is ripe – an eschatological parallel to Jesus' words that the fields are already white for harvest.

The Samaritans who came out of the city after the woman's testimony ([ref:Joh 4:29-30|John 4:29-30]) form the concrete background for Jesus' words about lifting one's eyes and seeing the fields – they represent the ripe harvest he points to.
The result of the harvest Jesus spoke of is shown in [ref:Joh 4:39-42|John 4:39-42], where many Samaritans came to believe – first through the woman's testimony, and then through Jesus' own words.
